section.title: Introduction and Overview
section.p: The DragASprite module was updated in RISC OS 4 to add a number to ease the use of the module. The rendering of the dragged object was updated in Select 2 to take advantage of the transparent rendering of sprites, making it easier to see where the object dragged was being placed.

subsection.title: Flags
subsection.p: The full bit flag set as used by R0 on entry to is as follows :

bitfield-table.bit:
Horizontal location of sprite in box (see PRM 3-301):
Left Centre Right Undefined

Vertical location of sprite in box (see PRM 3-301):
Bottom Centre Top Undefined

Drag bounding box is (see PRM 3-301):
Whole screen Display area of window that the pointer's over User specified Undefined

Bounding box applies to (see PRM 3-301):
The box The pointer

Control of drop-shadow (see PRM 3-301):
Don't do a drop-shadow Make a drop shadow when copying the sprite

Sprite transparency (see PRM 5a-493):
Sprite should be see-through Sprite should be solid

Sprite positioning (new to RISC OS 4):
Sprite's position is determined by bits 0-3 Sprite is centred on pointer position
Reserved for future use, should be set to 0

subsection.title: Rendering of the dragged sprite
subsection.p: The meaning of bit 8 changed slightly in Select 2. Under RISC OS 3.5 this bit was added to force the dragged image to be dithered with alternate masked pixels in a chequer-board pattern. Whilst this allowed the background to be dragged, it lost detail from the dragged sprite. This caused visual problems with sprites which used a dither pattern to make up their colours, such as the standard RISC OS sprite set.

Under Select 2 this behaviour was modified to use a true translucent sprite. However this effect is less effective as the number of colours in the display mode is reduced. At its extreme (2 colour modes) the sprite becomes solid. However, it is not expected that such low depths be used by many clients and so this is not a serious problem.
